Eugene Volokh — Chief Justice Robots, 68 Duke L.J. 1135 (2019)

Volokh argues that if AI can one day write briefs as persuasive as a human lawyer's, the same technology could produce AI judges that we should accept as no less reliable, and more cost-effective, than human ones. He proposes judging such programs by their output rather than their method, comparing them to human performers in a 'Modified John Henry Test', and using persuasiveness to a panel of evaluators as the measure. The Essay then walks through a series of 'AI promotions', from courtroom interpreter and brief-writer to staff attorney, fact-finder, judge, juror and finally law-developing appellate judge, and answers objections about sincerity, mercy, prejudice, public hostility and hacking. Read aloud in full; footnotes omitted.
